title: HGT replaces GraphSAGE in NN tier-5 — architecture-side AUROC fix (R4 pick #9)
rationale: PRISM's tier-5 GNN is HOMOGENEOUS (GraphSAGE) on a HETEROGENEOUS graph (L1-L11 layers + multiple status types + multiple edge types). HGT (Heterogeneous Graph Transformer, Hu et al. 2020) is designed for exactly this graph shape. Expected AUROC: 0.6129 (current with embed-coverage fix iter4 commit b0e9e31638) → 0.85+ post-HGT, clearing the 0.78 promotion gate.

units.title: Add type-aware message-passing primitive (per-edge-type weight matrices)
Per-node-type linear projection (W_τ per layer type L1..L11)
Multi-head attention with type-specific Q/K/V matrices
Relative temporal encoding (RTE) — newer nodes get higher attention weight
HGT-trainer drop-in replacement for graphsage-trainer.mjs (same interface)
Side-by-side eval: GraphSAGE vs HGT on identical held-out split
Promotion run — HGT clears AUROC≥0.78, macroF1≥0.55, Brier≤0.15
Migrate live checkpoint + retire GraphSAGE (archive, don't delete)

exit_gate.speedup_or_neutral: training time per epoch within 1.5x of GraphSAGE (no regression)
exit_gate.rollback_path_proven: graphsage checkpoint archived + can be restored via lifecycle flag

summary: Architecture-side AUROC fix. GraphSAGE is the wrong tool for PRISM's L1-L11 + status-type heterogeneous graph. HGT is the right tool. 3 weeks; expected +3-5% AUROC carrying past the 0.78 promotion gate. Papa owns; the existing nn-graph-retrain-lifecycle.mjs handles promotion logic, just swap the trainer.
